entries.style_notes: The official D&D species catalogue confirms Triton as an aquatic analogue but offers no public Merfolk naming convention; this is an original fluid, syllabic Fortcamp palette, not a claim that Merfolk are Tritons. Personal names work alone; optional family and harbor bynames imply no required ocean kingdom.

entries.style_notes: The D&D 2014 dragonborn rules verify personal names and honorific clan-first order; Fortcamp Dragonkin borrow that structural option without claiming the same biology or mandatory clan membership. Clipped and rolling draconic sounds have original short personal names and optional original clan names; titles are never inherited automatically.

entries.style_notes: Fortcamp Automata use shared self-chosen names that can be ordinary, material, vocational, or gently mechanical; D&D Warforged is a construct analogue in the consulted species directory, not identical setting lore or a confirmed naming rule. Optional workshop designations are meaningful labels rather than numbered stock-keeping codes, and both allowed genders use the same given-name pool.

entries.style_notes: The D&D Beyond species catalogue establishes Aasimar as mortals with Upper Planes ancestry, but supplies no verified single naming language in the consulted entry. Fortcamp Aasimar therefore receive varied mortal personal and family names with only a light lyrical undertone; no name automatically confers sainthood, divine office, prophecy or noble heritage.

Dragonkin: D&D 2014 confirms dragonborn personal and clan-first conventions; biological equivalence, exact sound choices, and Fortcamp clan systems are NOT sourced or asserted.
